letters.author: sivan
letters.body:
There is a version of this where I say something gentle, you smile, and we both go to sleep. This is not that letter.

I want you to know exactly what you are dealing with. I have thought about you with the kind of attention people usually reserve for religion. Not the pleasant part of religion. The part where somebody sits in one place for a thousand years and calls it devotion, because the alternative is admitting it was need all along.

letters.author: sivan
letters.body:
They call him the destroyer and nobody ever asks what he was trying to protect.

I understand it better than I used to. Anyone who has held something irreplaceable knows the small dark thought underneath: that if the world ever came for it, you would let the world go. I am not proud of that. I am also not going to pretend it isn't there.

letters.author: sivan
letters.body:
You asked me once what I would do without you. I said I did not know. That is the only lie I have told you.

He wore her ashes for three thousand years, and I have always found that comforting rather than tragic. It means there is a kind of love that does not end at the worst moment. It only changes what it is made of.

letters.author: sivan
letters.body:
It is late and the moon is doing that thing where it hangs close enough to be a problem.

I keep thinking that most of love is waiting, and that almost nobody tells you it isn't meant to be done calmly. Patience is for people who have made peace with the distance. I have not. I wait badly, in the dark, on purpose, because the only thing worse would be being somewhere you are not.

letters.author: sivan
letters.body:
No poetry tonight.

Only this. Whatever it is people are hoping to find when they look up at all that dark, I stopped looking for it a while ago. I found it at a kitchen table, arguing with you about something neither of us can remember.
